question: Which physicist's experiment during a lecture in 1820 showed the connection between electricity and magnetism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hans Christian Oersted**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hans Christian Oersted** was a Danish physicist and chemist.
 
• In 1820, during a lecture, he discovered that a compass needle is deflected by a nearby electric current, demonstrating a direct relationship between electricity and magnetism.
 
• This experiment laid the groundwork for the field of electromagnetism.
 
• Oersted's discovery showed that electric currents create magnetic fields, which was a major milestone in the study of physics.
 
• This connection between electricity and magnetism is fundamental to many modern technologies, including electric motors and transformers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hans Christian Oersted** was born on August 14, 1777, and died on March 9, 1851.
 
• He was also the first to isolate aluminum in 1825.
 
• Oersted's work influenced later scientists, including André-Marie Ampère, who further developed the theory of electromagnetism.
 
• The unit of magnetic field strength in the CGS system, the oersted (Oe), is named in his honor.
